chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, who said:

I asked Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about the lime (plaster) upon which faeces and the bones of the dead were burned, then the mosque is plastered with it. Can one perform prostration upon it? So he (peace be upon him) wrote to me in his own handwriting: 'The water and the fire have already purified it.'

key_terms.الْجِصِّ: Lime or gypsum plaster used for coating walls

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to pray on mosque walls plastered with lime that was burned with impurities?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Rida (AS) clarifies that the impurities (*najis*) of feces and bones are purified through the dual processes of burning (*al-nar*) and the application of plaster which involves moisture (*al-ma'*). This ruling is significant in Shia jurisprudence as it establishes that physical transformation and exposure to purifying elements can render a previously impure surface suitable for prayer (*Sajdah*), emphasizing the practicality of ritual purity in daily worship. The Imam’s direct response highlights the principle that *najis* materials do not remain permanently defiled if subjected to these specific purifying agents.
